subject.title: fix(agents): include requester identity in sessions_send context (Fixes #38570)

question: After reviewing a redacted real A2A run, should OpenClaw accept configured requester identity text as trusted, sanitized system-prompt context for `sessions_send` recipients?
rationale: The implementation adds configured identity text to a system prompt. The existing line sanitizer mitigates newline injection, but the protected human-review label requires an explicit owner decision on the remaining prompt-boundary and runtime-proof question.

options.title: Require live proof, then approve this narrow path
options.body: Keep the current plumbing and review a redacted two-agent runtime capture that shows initial, reply, and announce context receive the sanitized requester name.

options.title: Constrain identity exposure further
options.body: Require a different representation or explicit trust boundary if maintainers do not want configured identity text included in recipient system prompts.

recommendation.title: Require live proof, then approve this narrow path
recommendation.body: Keep the current plumbing and review a redacted two-agent runtime capture that shows initial, reply, and announce context receive the sanitized requester name.

likelyOwner.reason: They explicitly reopened the PR, acknowledged the earlier automation error, and applied the human-review protection now governing this item.
